idiom_name: reducing-function composition over Array.prototype.reduce / for..of, or the transducer protocol (transducers-js / transducers.js)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no stdlib transducer, but it supplies both necessary pieces: first-class functions and Array.prototype.reduce, so a reducing function is any (acc, x) => acc and a transducer is a one-liner - map(f) = rf => (acc, x) => rf(acc, f(x)) - composed with comp/pipe into a reusable transformation value whose sink is supplied at application time by the reducing function passed to reduce/transduce. Ready-made realisations follow the transducer protocol (Cognitect's transducers-js with @@transducer/init|result|step, toFn, transduce/into/comp; jlongster's transducers.js which also adapts arbitrary data structures such as Immutable.js), and since ES2025 iterator helpers, iter.map(...).filter(...).take(...) covers the lazy, source-agnostic case (iterators, generators, Set/Map iterators) without any library. What replaces the classic structure: plain function composition over reduce for in-process pipelines, and the protocol objects only when a library must accept third-party reducible types; the classic form is also the right answer when the same stack must feed a non-array sink such as a stream writer or a channel.
pitfalls: A bare reduce has no completion arity: buffering stages must flush in the terminal, and without a reduced wrapper take/drop stages keep consuming the source.
Stateful stages must be created per application - a closure-level prev in a module-level transducer is shared across executions, callers and awaits, silently mixing state.

Arrays and iterables behave differently: array methods are eager and hole-skipping, iterator helpers (Iterator.prototype.map/filter, Baseline 2025) are lazy and single-pass, and a transducer applied over an iterator cannot assume the source can be re-iterated.
